sections.html:
Goshen sits in northern Elkhart County near the Michigan line, and it is the county seat. The 2020 census counted 34,517 residents, and 69.2 percent of homes across Elkhart County are lived in by their owners. Recreational vehicle plants anchor the job market. When RV orders drop and layoffs follow, an owner may need cash and a closing date sooner than a listing can promise.

Prices and buyer interest shift from one block to the next. Picture a bungalow close to downtown, a ranch by the river and a newer build at the city's edge: three buyers, three different price conversations. We value each house by its condition and its location.

Platted in 1831, Goshen has downtown streets lined with houses more than a century old. Around the Goshen Historic District, expect wiring that mixes knob-and-tube with newer runs, original plumbing, plaster walls and foundations that have settled. A buyer relying on a mortgage usually asks you to correct those before closing, and that request is what drags a standard listing out.

Planning exterior work on a historic block? Ask the city first. Roofs, siding and windows all require permits, and that holds whether you do the work yourself or hand it to the next owner.

Owners of older houses can spend on wiring, plumbing and foundation to suit a financed buyer, or sell to a buyer who accepts the place unchanged. Collect a rough repair estimate under either plan, since it shows what a fair number looks like.

Winters in Goshen are cold and snowy, summers warm and humid, and a typical year brings about 45 inches of snow. Ice dams, heavy snow and repeated freezing and thawing take their toll on roofs, gutters and foundations. An aging furnace or water heater frequently becomes the item a buyer haggles over.

Water is the second worry. In February 2018 the Elkhart River climbed to 12.49 feet at Goshen, a record. A house close to the river or the old Millrace may have had water in its basement or crawlspace. Say so openly if yours did. Indiana's residential sales disclosure statute, IC 32-21-5, defines defects and provides the disclosure form.

sections.h2: City rules that touch a sale
sections.html:
Three city programs run through the Building Department: the building code, rental registration and the neighborhood preservation ordinance.

  • Roof, siding and window jobs need permits. So do additions and any new or changed electrical, plumbing or mechanical work, water heaters included.
  • Ordinances 4860 and 5001 require rentals to be registered and inspected. A landlord about to sell should check that registration is current.
  • The Neighborhood Preservation Ordinance reaches exterior items: paint, roofs, siding, porches and foundations.
  • A building decision can be appealed to the Board of Building Appeals within 15 days.

You can still sell with a violation on file. It may surface during the title search and worry a lender, though. Cash buyers can generally close with the violation unresolved, which saves you the cost and delay of curing it.

sections.h2: Property taxes and the sales disclosure form
sections.html:
Goshen owners pay Elkhart County property tax in a spring installment and a fall installment, falling on May 11 and November 10 under the 2026 schedule. A late payment adds 5 percent when made within 30 days of the due date, and 10 percent beyond that. Payment goes to the county treasurer. Selling in the fall? Ask the closing agent how the November bill will be divided between you and the buyer.

Most Indiana transfers also call for a sales disclosure form, signed by both sides. The county assessor reviews it, the auditor receives it ahead of the deed filing, and the recorder refuses a deed without proof the form arrived. The procedure has been revised over the years, so phone the county auditor for today's steps.

IC 32-21-5 adds a seller's disclosure form that should reach the buyer before an offer is accepted. Your title company will name the forms that apply. Tell them if the house is part of an estate, since estates add paperwork.

The sellers we hear from most often own aging houses, inherited homes, tenant-occupied rentals or houses that flooded. Each slows a traditional sale for its own reason.

  • Inherited houses: heirs frequently live elsewhere and want the sale done without repeat trips.
  • Rentals: tenants, registration and inspection must be sorted before showings are workable.
  • Flood or basement history: repair quotes can exceed what the owner expected.
  • Layoff or job change: swings in RV production can force a move ahead of any listing timeline.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to closing
sections.html:
1. Call or send your address and tell us about the house, any tenants and any open city notices.
  2. We look at the property and give you an offer.
  3. If you accept, we open the sale with a title company, which searches the deed for liens and unpaid taxes.
  4. You sign the sales disclosure form and the deed paperwork.
  5. The Elkhart County Recorder records the deed, and you collect your proceeds.

Any tax owed is paid out of the proceeds at closing, so it does not have to be settled in advance. If something turns up in the title search, the title company will explain it before closing day.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works here
sections.html:
We buy houses as-is. You contact us, we view the Goshen property, and our offer reflects what we see and where the house sits. If you accept, a title company or attorney clears the deed, prepares the sales disclosure form and fixes a closing date. No lender appraisal stands in the way, and you avoid repairs, cleanouts and open houses.

For the first conversation, gather any lease, your latest tax bill, mortgage payoff figures and any city notice about the property. Having them lets the title company spot trouble early. Get the closing date in writing and settle who pays which closing costs before signing.

This route does not fit every owner. Set the offer next to what listing would cost you: repair bills, showings and the monthly expense of carrying a house that has not sold.

faqs.q: How long does it take to sell a house in Goshen, IN for cash?
faqs.a: Title work and your own schedule set the pace, not repairs. With no lender appraisal, a cash closing can beat a financed one, but the title company still has to clear the deed and process the Indiana disclosure form. Request the closing date in writing.

faqs.q: Do I need to fix code violations before selling in Goshen?
faqs.a: No law makes you cure one before a sale, though it may turn up in the title search and trouble a lender. The Goshen Building Department, 574-534-1811, can tell you what is open on your address. Cash buyers can often take the house with the issue unresolved.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Goshen rental with tenants in place?
faqs.a: Yes, and the lease stays with the property. Goshen requires registered, inspected rentals, so verify your registration. Give any buyer the lease terms on rent, deposit and length.

faqs.q: When are Elkhart County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Two installments a year, one in May and one in November. Paying within 30 days late costs 5 percent, and later than that costs 10 percent. Pay your county treasurer.

faqs.q: Does flood history have to be disclosed in Goshen?
faqs.a: A past water problem is something a buyer will want to hear, and IC 32-21-5 sets up the disclosure form. Ask your agent or attorney how to describe your own house.
